text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a sustained p99 token-gen increase on a subset of US-WEST racks since 03:10 UTC. p50 fine, p99 jumped from ~2.8s -> 4.3s and GPU util on those hosts is pegged at 98%.

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-util-high on rack-usw2-r18 (hosts: 18.22.3.*). See: https://telemetry.internal/alerts/ALRT-6523

priya: Logs show a lot of TCP retransmits from the proxy side around the same time. NIC RX errors spike. pasted relevant netstat: `tcp_retransmits: 1200` (short window).

matt: curious if this is KV cache spill + egress saturation combo. When kv-regen happens we see big spikes in PCIe and pcie stall counters.

sasha: can we confirm which tenants landed on those hosts? I saw two heavy RLHF training tenants + a low-latency chat tenant. That combo is unfortunate.

alex: yeah, tenant list: tenant-a (rlhf), tenant-b (batch rerank), tenant-c (chat). tenant-a and tenant-b share the same slice.

dana: if we push tenant-a to a fractional dedicated slice we'll burn extra committed capacity — need cost estimate before we do any manual carveouts.

priya: quick probe: `ssh rack-usw2-r18-22 'nvidia-smi dmon -s u'` output looks like sustained encode spikes on GPU0-3. Also `ethtool -S eth0` shows rx_no_buf increments. Might be driver-level NIC pressure.

matt: +1 on NIC pressure. I tracked similar incidents where vGPU tenants caused DMA bursts that starved NIC queues. Could be the shared host IO path.

sasha: short remediation options: 1) Shadow-drain tenant-a to warm fractional dedicated pool (low friction), 2) Enable egress shaping for the slice (rate cap), 3) Soft-preempt tenant-b batch jobs for 10m. Which order do we want?

alex: prefer 2 then 1; shaping is fastest. How practical to apply per-slice egress shaping now?

priya: we have an emergency knob: `egress.police.slices.usw2=true` in the allocator config. I can flip it but it'll affect any slice using default egress. We can target the specific slice id: `slice-7823`.

dana: before flipping, what's the expected cost delta if we instead migrate tenant-a to dedicated? Rough ballpark per-hour?

matt: tenant-a uses ~12 GPU-hours/hr when hot. Dedicated fractional carveout for that profile ~$1.8/hr plus prefill overhead. But migration friction + warmup could cause 5-15% extra token cost for 30m.

sasha: timeline: shaping flip -> 2 min to propagate -> should see immediate RX drops if it's egress-bound. If no improvement, start background migration to dedicated warm pool and throttled handoff.

priya: flipping now would be: `POST /allocator/config -d '{"slice_id":"slice-7823","egress_cap_mbps":350}'` (we're currently at ~900Mbps observed).

alex: go ahead if you think safe. @matt can you start a canary migration plan in parallel? document steps here so SRE on call can follow.

matt: will do. Canary plan (short):
```
1) mark tenant-a as migrate:candidate
2) create dedicated fractional slice with 2x observed burst headroom
3) warm KV cache by replaying last 10m traffic in warm-pool (rate-limited)
4) flip routing weight: 10%->50%->100% over 5,10,20m windows
5) monitor p99 and rx_errs; rollback if p99 increases >10% on destination
```

infra-bot: NOTE: allocator-change requested by priya at 1876543384. Change queued.

sasha: also consider short-term NIC firmware throttle? We've seen ethtool coalescing tweaks help with rx_no_buf in past incidents. Might reduce jitter.

priya: applied egress cap to slice-7823 -> cap 350mbps. propagation 90s.

alex: seeing initial drop in RX errors on hosts 18.22.3.*. p99 trending down to 3.2s after 3m. good sign.

dana: cost watch — if we keep dedicated for more than 6 hours we should pre-approve. Otherwise shaping + soft-preempt should be enough.

matt: starting canary migration: creating pool id `ded-slice-0821` now, will kick warmup jobs. ETA first 10% traffic shift 10m.

sasha: if warmup doesn't fill KV quickly we might see QoS regressions due to cold-start. plan to replay hashed prompt keys only.

priya: telemetry shows PCIe stall counters reduced post-shaping too. That suggests KV regen spike was partially caused by egress-induced backpressure.

alex: ok team — keep monitoring for the next 30m. If p99 stabilizes below 3.0s and RX stays low we can avoid carveout. If not, proceed with migration and loop back to product about cost.

matt: filing a short post-incident runbook draft with lessons and a new pre-emptive play (egress pre-checks before warmpool placement). I'll paste when done.

sasha: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

infra-bot: RESOLVED: alert ALRT-6523 closed at 1876543899 (p99 recovered).
